q: Ankit asks an AI for a formula and pastes it, but it shows #NAME? on his office laptop. What should he have told the AI upfront?
options: The colour formatting used in his sheet
The name of his manager and department
Which Excel or Sheets version he is using
How many people will open the file
explain: Functions like XLOOKUP only exist in newer versions, so always tell the AI your tool and version.

q: Which request is most likely to get a correct, paste-ready SUMIFS formula from an AI on the first try?
options: One that gives the sheet name, column letters, data types, version, sample rows and expected result
One that simply says "Give me a formula to total Jaipur sales"
One that uploads the full workbook with all customer details included
One that asks the AI to guess the column layout from the file name
explain: The CONTEXT template (layout, output, value types, tool, examples, exceptions) lets the AI write a formula for your actual sheet.

q: Deepa needs to upload sales data to analyse category growth. Her copy has a hidden Customer Mobile column. What should she do?
options: Leave it hidden, since hidden columns are not uploaded
Mask the numbers to show only the first four digits
Rename the column header so the AI ignores it
Delete the column from the copy, because hidden columns still upload
explain: Share the minimum: delete unneeded columns from a copy, since hidden columns are still included in the upload.

q: A colleague's file uses =VLOOKUP(C2, Products!A:D, 3, FALSE). Why does the course suggest avoiding this in new work?
options: VLOOKUP cannot return text values, only numbers
VLOOKUP only works in Google Sheets, not Excel
VLOOKUP always requires the data to be sorted
Inserting a column in Products silently makes the 3 point at the wrong data
explain: VLOOKUP's fixed column index goes stale when columns are inserted, with no warning.

q: An XLOOKUP returns #N/A for "SR-102" even though the code is visible in the master list. What is a likely cause to check first?
options: The master list has too many rows for XLOOKUP
A hidden trailing space or a number stored as text
XLOOKUP needs the data sorted in ascending order
The formula needs to be converted to VLOOKUP
explain: Most #N/A errors come from extra spaces or text-versus-number mismatches; LEN and ISNUMBER help confirm them.

q: An AI gives a LinkedIn win-rate formula and the result is exactly 100%. What should you suspect?
options: The denominator is wrong, possibly identical to the numerator
LinkedIn really is the best-performing lead source
COUNTIFS cannot calculate percentages correctly
The cells need to be formatted as percentages
explain: A suspicious 100% often means a copy-paste slip in the denominator; win rate should divide Won by Won plus Lost.

q: An inherited SUMPRODUCT formula uses ranges ending at row 5000 and the monthly number now looks low. What is the best next step?
options: Check the last used row with Ctrl + End to see if data now exceeds row 5000
Wrap the formula in another IFERROR to remove any errors
Delete the formula and type the number in manually
Ask the AI to confirm the number and send the report
explain: Treat the AI's explanation as hypotheses and test them; a fixed range that misses newer rows is a likely cause.

q: Pink City Fabrics' data has some identical item lines. Before removing duplicates, what should you decide first?
options: Which colour to highlight the duplicates in
What combination of columns makes a row truly unique
Whether to delete the oldest or newest rows
How many duplicates the manager expects to see
explain: Not every repeated row is a duplicate, so define the unique key (such as Invoice No + Item Code) first.

q: Rohit adds new rows to his pivot table's source data, but the pivot totals don't change. What most likely went wrong?
options: Pivot tables cannot include more than 1,000 rows
The new rows need to be typed directly into the pivot
He did not refresh the pivot, or the source is a fixed range
He should have used a calculated field instead
explain: Pivots need a refresh, and a fixed source range silently ignores rows beyond it; an Excel Table avoids that.

q: The owner asks for average invoice value, but the data has one row per item line. What should you do?
options: Average the Amount column directly across all item lines
Divide total sales by the number of item lines
Ask the AI to estimate it from a sample of rows
Total each invoice first, then average the invoice totals
explain: This is a grain issue: line-level data must be aggregated to invoice level before invoice metrics.

q: In a recurring monthly MIS report, what is the main benefit of using Power Query to combine and clean branch files?
options: Cleaning steps are recorded once and replayed on every refresh
It removes the need to check totals each month
It lets you type corrections directly into the pivot tables
It automatically writes the commentary for the report
explain: Power Query records each step, so next month you add files and click Refresh All.

q: After uploading a CSV to a chat assistant with data analysis, what should your first prompt do?
options: Ask for five key insights and a summary chart
Ask it to predict next quarter's sales
Ask it to describe the data back: rows, columns, types, date range and distinct values
Ask it to write the executive email for your manager
explain: An orientation prompt catches misreads, such as DD/MM parsed as MM/DD, before they affect every answer.

q: An AI's category breakdown sums to ₹48.2 lakh, but total sales are ₹51.0 lakh. What does this most likely indicate?
options: The AI rounded each category to the nearest lakh
Some rows were dropped, often blanks or an unexpected spelling
GST was added to the category totals by mistake
The total sales figure in Excel must be wrong
explain: Parts should add up to the whole; a shortfall usually means silent filtering of blanks or variant spellings.

q: A number from AI analysis will be used in a board deck. What does the course recommend?
options: Use it as is if the AI showed its code
Ask the AI the same question twice and average the results
Round it to the nearest lakh to reduce the chance of error
Use AI to find the insight, then rebuild the figure in your own workbook
explain: For consequential numbers, rebuild them with formulas or pivots you control and keep an audit note.

q: AI-written pandas code reads Indian DD-MM-YYYY dates. What should you check it includes?
options: A line that deletes rows with any blank values
dayfirst=True when converting the date column
A command to sort the file by date first
A setting that converts dates to text labels
explain: dayfirst=True makes pandas read Indian dates correctly; also count values that failed to parse.

q: In Power BI, you want an FYTD sales total for an Indian financial year. What must the TOTALYTD measure include?
options: A filter that removes January to March data
A calculated column instead of a measure
A year-end date argument of "3/31"
A separate table for each financial year
explain: Without the "3/31" year-end argument, TOTALYTD resets every January instead of every April.

q: Which chart choice best follows the course's dashboard guidance for comparing sales across eight categories?
options: A pie chart with eight slices
A 3D column chart in category name order
A horizontal bar chart sorted largest first with data labels
A gauge showing each category separately
explain: Category comparisons work best as sorted horizontal bars with direct labels; avoid many-slice pies and 3D charts.

q: An AI-drafted executive summary says sales rose "because of the influencer campaign", which you never verified. What should you do?
options: Change it to neutral wording like "coinciding with" or remove it
Keep it, since the AI may have found a pattern you missed
Add a percentage to make the claim more convincing
Move it to the headline so the director notices it
explain: Unverified causal claims must be softened or removed; give the AI only verified facts and check every claim.
